source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 15 (PDF 25-56, printed 25-56); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 15 (Human Nervous System), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 In humans, chemical coordination is controlled by the:
blocks.explanation: Humans have two types of coordination: nervous coordination (nervous system) and chemical coordination (endocrine system).

book_ref.quote: Chemical coordination controlled by the endocrine system

blocks.prompt: 2 Nervous coordination is carried out by means of:
blocks.explanation: In nervous coordination the nervous system works by means of electrical signals.

book_ref.quote: Nervous coordination is done by means of electrical signals

blocks.prompt: 3 Receptors are called transducers because they:

options.text: convert one form of energy into another form

blocks.explanation: Receptors convert one form of energy into another, e.g. rods and cones of the retina convert light energy into nerve impulses.

book_ref.quote: Receptors act as transducers because they convert one form of energy into another form

blocks.prompt: 4 The brain and spinal cord are made of which neurons that process incoming impulses?
blocks.explanation: The CNS is made of associative neurons (inter-neurons) that receive impulses from sensory neurons and process them.

book_ref.quote: These parts are made of associative neurons (also called inter-neurons)

blocks.prompt: 5 Glands act as effectors by:
blocks.explanation: Muscles respond by contracting while glands respond by producing secretion.

book_ref.quote: Muscles produce response by contracting while glands produce secretion

blocks.prompt: 6 The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the:
blocks.explanation: A neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

book_ref.quote: A neuron is the structural and functional unit of nervous system

blocks.prompt: 7 Which cells supply nutrients to neurons, remove wastes and provide immunity?
blocks.explanation: The supporting cells of the nervous system, neuroglia or glial cells, have these functions.

book_ref.quote: They supply nutrients to neurons, remove wastes, and provide immunity

blocks.prompt: 8 The myelin sheath around axons in the central nervous system is produced by:
blocks.explanation: Schwann cells make myelin in the peripheral nervous system; oligodendrocytes make it in the CNS.

book_ref.quote: Oligodendrocytes produce myelin sheath in central nervous system

blocks.prompt: 9 In myelinated neurons, nodes of Ranvier occur at intervals of about:
blocks.explanation: The myelin sheath is interrupted every 1 to 2 mm by small non-myelinated gaps called nodes of Ranvier.

book_ref.quote: the myelin sheath is interrupted at intervals of 1 to 2 mm by small gaps

blocks.prompt: 10 In the CNS, white matter is made of:
blocks.explanation: In the CNS myelinated axons make white matter; non-myelinated dendrites and cell bodies make grey matter.

book_ref.quote: In the CNS, myelinated axons make white matter

blocks.prompt: 11 Nissl's granules in the cell body of a neuron are groups of:
blocks.explanation: The cytoplasm of the cell body has Nissl's granules, which are groups of ribosomes and rough ER.

book_ref.quote: These are group of ribosomes and rough endoplasmic reticulum

blocks.prompt: 12 Motor neurons and inter-neurons have highly branched dendrites because they:

options.text: receive impulses from many sources simultaneously
carry impulses away from the cell body

blocks.explanation: Motor and inter-neurons receive impulses from many different sources at the same time, so their dendrites are highly branched.

book_ref.quote: That is why, they possess highly branched dendrites

blocks.prompt: 13 The axons controlling the muscles of human feet can be:
blocks.explanation: Axons controlling the muscles in the feet are more than a meter long (in a giraffe, skull to pelvis axons are about three metres).

book_ref.quote: the axons controlling the muscles in your feet are more than a meter long

blocks.prompt: 14 The end of an axon that may contact a muscle cell, gland cell or another neuron is the:
blocks.explanation: The end of an axon is the axon terminal; it may contact a muscle cell, a gland cell or another neuron.

book_ref.quote: The end of an axon is called the axon terminal

blocks.prompt: 15 The cell bodies of sensory neurons are located:

options.text: in the grey matter of spinal cord

blocks.explanation: Cell bodies of sensory neurons lie outside the CNS in clusters called ganglia.

book_ref.quote: Their cell bodies are located outside of the CNS in the form of clusters called ganglia

blocks.prompt: 16 Motor neurons are described as:
blocks.explanation: Motor neurons are multipolar: they have many dendrites branching into smaller dendrites.

book_ref.quote: They are multipolar. It means that they have many dendrites

blocks.prompt: 17 Which neurons occur entirely within the CNS?
blocks.explanation: Inter-neurons (associative neurons) occur entirely within the CNS.

book_ref.quote: Inter-neurons (associative neurons) occur entirely within the CNS

blocks.prompt: 18 Inter-neurons with short axons:

options.text: form circuits with nearby neurons to analyse small information
connect distant regions of brain and spinal cord

blocks.explanation: Short-axon inter-neurons form circuits with nearby neurons; long-axon ones connect different regions of the brain and spinal cord.

book_ref.quote: Some inter-neurons have short axons and form circuits with nearby neurons

blocks.prompt: 19 The simplest neural pathway in the nervous system is the:
blocks.explanation: The reflex arc is the simplest neural pathway; it controls immediate, automatic and involuntary responses.

book_ref.quote: The reflex arc is the simplest neural pathway

blocks.prompt: 20 In the knee-jerk reflex, the stimulus (tapping) is sensed by a receptor present in the:
blocks.explanation: Tapping the patellar tendon is sensed by a receptor in the quadriceps muscle of the thigh.

book_ref.quote: This stimulus (tapping) is sensed by a receptor present in the quadriceps muscle of thigh

blocks.prompt: 21 In the knee-jerk reflex, the sensory neuron passes the impulse to the motor neuron of quadriceps:
blocks.explanation: In the spinal cord the sensory neuron transfers the impulse to a motor neuron without involving an inter-neuron.

book_ref.quote: the sensory neuron transfers the impulse to a motor neuron without involving an inter-neuron

blocks.prompt: 22 During the knee-jerk, the hamstrings muscle:

options.text: is stimulated by the sensory neuron directly
relaxes because an inter-neuron inhibits its motor neurons

blocks.explanation: The sensory neuron also activates an inter-neuron that inhibits the motor neurons of the hamstrings, so the hamstrings relax.

book_ref.quote: It results in the relaxation of hamstrings during the extension of the lower leg

blocks.prompt: 23 A wave of electrochemical changes travelling along the length of a neuron is a:
blocks.explanation: A nerve impulse is a wave of electrochemical changes that travels along the length of a neuron.

book_ref.quote: A nerve impulse is defined as a wave of electrochemical changes

blocks.prompt: 24 The membrane potentials of which cells can change because they can change the rates of ion movement?
blocks.explanation: In most cells ion movement is constant; muscle cells and neurons can change it, so their membrane potentials change.

book_ref.quote: the cell membranes of muscle and neurons can change the rates of ions movements

blocks.text: 15.3.1 Generation and Transmission of Nerve Impulse

blocks.prompt: 25 The resting membrane potential of a neuron is about:
blocks.explanation: The RMP of a polarized neuron is about –70 millivolts; the negative sign shows the inside is negative to the outside.

book_ref.quote: it is about –70 millivolts (–70 mV)

blocks.prompt: 26 In a resting neuron, the concentration of K⁺ inside compared with outside is about:
blocks.explanation: K⁺ is 30 times more concentrated inside; Na⁺ is 10 times more concentrated outside.

book_ref.quote: The concentration of K⁺ is 30 times greater inside the neuron than outside

blocks.prompt: 27 In each cycle, the sodium-potassium pump moves:
blocks.explanation: For every two K⁺ actively transported inward, three Na⁺ are pumped out, so the inside becomes more negative.

book_ref.quote: For every two K⁺ that are actively transported inward, three Na⁺ are pumped out

blocks.prompt: 28 Large negatively charged molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids that cannot diffuse out of a neuron are called:
blocks.explanation: These large negative molecules are more abundant inside and cannot diffuse out; they are called fixed anions.

book_ref.quote: These molecules are called fixed anions

blocks.prompt: 29 During depolarization, the membrane potential changes from –70 mV towards zero and then reaches about:
blocks.explanation: Na⁺ rushes in; the potential changes from –70 mV towards zero and then reaches 50 mV.

book_ref.quote: towards zero and then reaches to 50 mV

blocks.prompt: 30 Depolarization produces an action potential on a short region of a neuron for about:
blocks.explanation: The action potential at a region lasts about one millisecond.

book_ref.quote: This depolarization produces action potential on a short region of neuron for about one millisecond

blocks.prompt: 31 Repolarization of the neuron membrane occurs when:

options.text: Na⁺ gates open and Na⁺ rushes in
Na⁺ gates close and K⁺ gates open, so K⁺ diffuses out
Cl⁻ channels open and Cl⁻ enters
Ca²⁺ gates open and Ca²⁺ enters

blocks.explanation: After depolarization, Na⁺ gates close and K⁺ gates open; K⁺ diffuses out and the inside becomes negative again.

book_ref.quote: Na⁺ gates close and the K⁺ gates open

blocks.prompt: 32 Hyperpolarization of a neuron is due to:

options.text: slight delay in closing all the K⁺ gates

blocks.explanation: Hyperpolarization (slightly more negative than RMP) is due to the slight delay in closing all the K⁺ gates.

book_ref.quote: It is due to the slight delay in closing all the K⁺ gates

blocks.prompt: 33 After the refractory period, the original ionic distribution of the neuron is restored by:
blocks.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump restores the original ion distribution and the membrane returns to RMP (–70 mV).

book_ref.quote: original ionic distribution is restored by sodium-potassium pump

blocks.prompt: 34 An action potential moves along an axon because:

options.text: the same ions flow from one end to the other
each action potential depolarizes the next region, which produces its own

blocks.explanation: Action potentials are reproduced: one region's action potential is the depolarization stimulus for the next region.

book_ref.quote: An action potential in a region of axon serves as a depolarization stimulus for the next region

blocks.prompt: 35 Along the length of an axon, the amplitude of action potentials:
blocks.explanation: The action potential at the end of the axon is as strong as the first; only its velocity may vary.

book_ref.quote: The strength (amplitude) of action potentials remains constant along the length of axon

blocks.prompt: 36 In humans, non-myelinated neurons conduct impulses at a speed of:
blocks.explanation: Non-myelinated neurons conduct at 1 to 3 m/s; myelinated neurons at up to 120 m/s.

book_ref.quote: the non-myelinated neurons conduct impulses at speed of 1 to 3 metres per second

blocks.prompt: 37 Myelinated neurons in humans conduct impulses at speeds of up to:
blocks.explanation: Myelinated neurons conduct impulses at speeds of up to 120 metres per second.

book_ref.quote: the myelinated neurons conduct at speeds of up to 120 meters per second

blocks.prompt: 38 Saltatory conduction is faster than conduction in the fastest non-myelinated axons by up to:
blocks.explanation: Saltatory conduction is up to 50 times faster than impulses in the fastest non-myelinated axons.

book_ref.quote: It is up to 50 times faster than the nerve impulse through the fastest non-myelinated axons

blocks.prompt: 39 The fluid-filled gap between two neurons at a synapse is the:
blocks.explanation: At a synapse the two cells are not in direct contact; there is a fluid-filled gap called the synaptic cleft.

book_ref.quote: there is a fluid-filled gap between them, called a synaptic cleft

blocks.prompt: 40 The synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre is called:
blocks.explanation: A synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre is also called a neuro-muscular junction.

book_ref.quote: The synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre is also called neuro-muscular junction

blocks.prompt: 41 The neuron whose axon carries action potentials towards a synapse is the:
blocks.explanation: The neuron sending action potentials towards the synapse is presynaptic; the cell on the other side is postsynaptic.

book_ref.quote: The neuron whose axon transmits action potentials towards synapse is the presynaptic neuron

blocks.prompt: 42 Synaptic vesicles in the synaptic knobs are packed with:
blocks.explanation: Synaptic knobs contain numerous synaptic vesicles packed with neurotransmitters.

book_ref.quote: These knobs contain numerous synaptic vesicles which are packed with chemicals called neurotransmitters

blocks.prompt: 43 Neurotransmitters are released from synaptic vesicles by:
blocks.explanation: Vesicles fuse with the presynaptic membrane and release neurotransmitters by exocytosis.

book_ref.quote: This fusion causes the release of neurotransmitters from vesicles by exocytosis

blocks.prompt: 44 The amount of neurotransmitter released at a synapse increases when:

options.text: the postsynaptic cell has fewer receptors
the frequency of action potentials in the presynaptic axon increases

blocks.explanation: The higher the frequency of action potentials in the presynaptic axon, the more neurotransmitter is released.

book_ref.quote: The higher the frequency of action potentials in the presynaptic axon, the more neurotransmitters are released

blocks.prompt: 45 After their action, used neurotransmitters are removed from the synaptic cleft by:

options.text: reabsorption by the presynaptic neuron or breakdown by enzymes

blocks.explanation: At many synapses used neurotransmitters are reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron; at others enzymes break them down.

book_ref.quote: At other synapses, they are broken down by enzymes

blocks.prompt: 46 Excitatory neurotransmitters generate action potentials in postsynaptic neurons by increasing membrane permeability to:
blocks.explanation: Excitatory neurotransmitters generate nerve impulses by increasing membrane permeability to Na⁺.

book_ref.quote: by increasing membrane permeability to Na⁺

blocks.prompt: 47 Which excitatory neurotransmitter is mentioned as acting in the CNS?
blocks.explanation: Glutamate is an excitatory neurotransmitter acting in the CNS; glycine, GABA and endorphins are inhibitory.

book_ref.quote: Glutamate acts in the CNS.

blocks.prompt: 48 Degeneration of which neurons produces the muscle tremors of Parkinson's disease?
blocks.explanation: Degeneration of dopamine-releasing neurons produces the muscle tremors of Parkinson's disease.

book_ref.quote: Degeneration of dopamine-releasing neurons produces the muscle tremors of Parkinson’s disease

blocks.prompt: 49 Many antidepressant drugs reduce depression by:

options.text: blocking the elimination of serotonin from the synaptic cleft

blocks.explanation: Insufficient serotonin activity may cause depression; antidepressants keep serotonin in the cleft by blocking its elimination.

book_ref.quote: Many antidepressant drugs block the elimination of serotonin from the synaptic cleft

blocks.prompt: 50 Which biogenic amine, made in the CNS and sympathetic nerves, regulates sleep patterns, focus and alertness?
blocks.explanation: Norepinephrine is made in the CNS and sympathetic nerves and regulates sleep patterns, focus and alertness.

book_ref.quote: It regulates sleep patterns, focus and alertness

blocks.prompt: 51 The brain neurotransmitter that controls body movements and pleasures related to motivation is:
blocks.explanation: Dopamine controls body movements, pleasures related to motivation and emotional stimulation.

book_ref.quote: It controls body movements, pleasures related to motivation and also emotional stimulation

blocks.prompt: 52 When an inhibitory neurotransmitter binds to the postsynaptic receptors, which channels open?
blocks.explanation: Chloride channels open instead of sodium channels; Cl⁻ enters and makes the inside more negative than RMP.

book_ref.quote: channels for chloride ions open instead of opening sodium channels

blocks.prompt: 53 The chief inhibitory neurotransmitter in the CNS is:
blocks.explanation: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the chief inhibitory neurotransmitter in the CNS; it reduces anxiety and promotes sleep.

book_ref.quote: is the chief inhibitory neurotransmitter in CNS

blocks.prompt: 54 Glycine acts as an inhibitory neurotransmitter especially in the:
blocks.explanation: Glycine is inhibitory especially in the spinal cord, brainstem and retina.

book_ref.quote: Glycine is an inhibitory neurotransmitter especially in the spinal cord, brainstem, and retina

blocks.prompt: 55 Many sedative drugs work by:

options.text: enhancing the binding of GABA to its receptors

blocks.explanation: Many sedatives enhance GABA binding to its receptors and so increase GABA's effectiveness at the synapse.

book_ref.quote: Many sedative drugs enhance the binding of GABA to its receptors

blocks.prompt: 56 Opium, morphine and heroin have an analgesic effect because they are chemically similar to:
blocks.explanation: They resemble endorphins in chemical structure and easily bind to endorphin receptors.

book_ref.quote: because they are similar in chemical structure to endorphins

blocks.prompt: 57 Nerve gases such as sarin, tabun and soman are toxic because they inhibit:
blocks.explanation: Nerve gas inhibits acetylcholinesterase, so acetylcholine accumulates and skeletal muscles stay contracted.

book_ref.quote: A nerve gas (e.g., sarin, tabun, soman) is a highly toxic chemical that inhibits this enzyme

blocks.prompt: 58 In nerve gas poisoning, breathing stops mainly because:
blocks.explanation: Accumulated acetylcholine keeps muscles contracted; if the diaphragm stays contracted, the person cannot breathe.

book_ref.quote: If the diaphragm muscle remains contracted, the person is not be able to breathe

blocks.text: 15.5 Basic organization of human nervous system

blocks.prompt: 59 The peripheral nervous system consists of:
blocks.explanation: The PNS consists of cranial and spinal nerves arising from the brain and spinal cord respectively.

book_ref.quote: The PNS consists of cranial and spinal nerves

blocks.text: 15.5.1 Central Nervous System - Brain & Spinal Cord

blocks.prompt: 60 The outermost thick layer of the meninges that contains larger blood vessels is the:
blocks.explanation: The dura mater, below the skull and vertebrae, is the outermost thick layer and contains larger blood vessels.

book_ref.quote: It contains larger blood vessels.

blocks.prompt: 61 The meningeal layer that acts as a barrier between cerebrospinal fluid and the blood of the dura mater is the:
blocks.explanation: The thin arachnoid lies below the dura mater and separates CSF below it from the blood in the dura mater.

book_ref.quote: It acts as a barrier between the cerebrospinal fluid present below it and the blood in the dura mater

blocks.prompt: 62 The average adult human brain weighs about:
blocks.explanation: The average adult human brain weighs 1.4 kg, about 2 percent of total body weight.

book_ref.quote: The average adult human brain weighs 1.4 kg (about 2 percent of total body weight)

blocks.prompt: 63 The two cerebral hemispheres are connected at the base of the deep groove by the:
blocks.explanation: At the base of the deep fissure the hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum, a band of axons.

book_ref.quote: both cerebral hemispheres are connected by the corpus callosum (a band of axons)

blocks.prompt: 64 Damage to the left cerebral hemisphere would cause loss of sensation and paralysis on the:
blocks.explanation: Each hemisphere serves the opposite side of the body, so damage to one causes loss on the opposite side.

book_ref.quote: Damage to one hemisphere results in a loss of sensation and paralysis on the opposite side of body

blocks.prompt: 65 Executive functions such as self-control, planning, reasoning and abstract thought are associated with the:
blocks.explanation: The frontal lobes are associated with executive functions including self-control, planning, reasoning and abstract thought.

book_ref.quote: The frontal lobes are associated with executive functions

blocks.prompt: 66 Vision is controlled by the:
blocks.explanation: The occipital lobes control vision; the visual cortex lies in the occipital lobe.

book_ref.quote: The occipital lobes control vision.

blocks.prompt: 67 The auditory cortex, which deals with different sound frequencies, lies in the:
blocks.explanation: The auditory cortex lies within the temporal lobe; the visual cortex lies in the occipital lobe.

book_ref.quote: A specialized area called auditory cortex within the temporal lobe deals with different sound frequencies

blocks.prompt: 68 A shallow groove separating gyri of the cerebral hemispheres is called a:
blocks.explanation: Ridges are gyri; a shallow groove is a sulcus and a deep groove is a fissure.

book_ref.quote: A shallow groove is called sulcus (plural, sulci) and a deep groove is called fissure

blocks.prompt: 69 The sites of higher mental activities in the cerebral cortex are the:
blocks.explanation: Association areas are the sites of higher mental activities, e.g. language on the left and visual-spatial ability on the right.

book_ref.quote: Association areas of the cortex are the sites of higher mental activities

blocks.prompt: 70 The part of the brainstem that transmits impulses between the cerebral hemispheres and cerebellum is the:
blocks.explanation: The pons transmits impulses between the cerebral hemispheres and the cerebellum.

book_ref.quote: Pons: It transmits impulses between the cerebral hemispheres and cerebellum

blocks.prompt: 71 The control centre for heart rate and respiration rate is the:
blocks.explanation: The medulla oblongata is a relay centre and a control centre for heart rate, respiration rate and other homeostatic activities.

book_ref.quote: serves as both a relay centre and a control centre for heart rate, respiration rate

blocks.prompt: 72 The reticular formation, which connects hindbrain with forebrain, is contained in the:
blocks.explanation: The midbrain relays visual and auditory information and contains the reticular formation.

book_ref.quote: It also contains reticular formation, which connects hindbrain with forebrain

blocks.prompt: 73 The relay centre between sensory information and the cerebrum is the:
blocks.explanation: The thalamus, part of the diencephalon, relays sensory information to the cerebrum.

book_ref.quote: Thalamus is a relay centre between sensory information and the cerebrum

blocks.prompt: 74 The part of the diencephalon that regulates body temperature, hunger and thirst and controls the pituitary gland is the:
blocks.explanation: The hypothalamus integrates visceral activities and controls the pituitary gland.

book_ref.quote: It also controls the pituitary gland

blocks.prompt: 75 The hormone melatonin, which controls sleep patterns, is produced by the:
blocks.explanation: The pineal gland, where the two halves of the thalamus join, produces melatonin.

book_ref.quote: It produces a hormone melatonin which controls sleep patterns

blocks.prompt: 76 Feelings and emotions of love, hate, anger and fear are controlled by the almond-shaped:
blocks.explanation: The amygdalae are two almond-shaped structures deep in the temporal lobes that control these emotions.

book_ref.quote: The amygdalae (singular: amygdala) are two almond-shaped structures

blocks.prompt: 77 The consolidation of information from short-term to long-term memory involves the:
blocks.explanation: The hippocampus, two horns curving back from the amygdala, consolidates short-term memory into long-term memory.

book_ref.quote: It plays role in the consolidation of information from short-term memory to long-term memory

blocks.prompt: 78 The part of the brain that processes information about body position and controls posture is the:
blocks.explanation: The cerebellum receives sensory impulses from muscles, tendons, joints, eyes and ears and controls posture.

book_ref.quote: It processes information about body position and controls posture

blocks.prompt: 79 The number of ventricles in the human brain is:
blocks.explanation: There are four ventricles: two lateral ventricles in the cerebrum, the third in the diencephalon and the fourth between cerebellum and brainstem.

book_ref.quote: There are four ventricles in human brain

blocks.prompt: 80 The main function of the ventricles of the brain is:

options.text: production and circulation of cerebrospinal fluid

blocks.explanation: The main function of the ventricles is the production and circulation of cerebrospinal fluid.

book_ref.quote: The main function of ventricles is the production and circulation of cerebrospinal fluid

blocks.prompt: 81 In the spinal cord, the inner H-shaped (butterfly-shaped) zone is made of:
blocks.explanation: The arrangement is opposite to the brain: inner H-shaped grey matter and outer white matter.

book_ref.quote: The inner H-shaped or butterfly-shaped zone is made of grey matter

blocks.prompt: 82 The diameter of the human spinal cord is between:
blocks.explanation: The spinal cord is 0.25 to 0.5 inch in diameter, wider in cervical and lumbar regions.

book_ref.quote: The diameter of spinal cord is between 0.25 to 0.5 inch

blocks.prompt: 83 The central canal of the spinal cord is a continuation of the:
blocks.explanation: The central fluid-filled canal of the spinal cord continues from the fourth ventricle of the brain.

book_ref.quote: It is a continuation of the fourth ventricle of brain

blocks.text: 15.5.2 Peripheral Nervous System - Cranial & Spinal Nerves

blocks.prompt: 84 Aggregations of cell bodies located outside the CNS are called:
blocks.explanation: Nerves are cable-like collections of axons; ganglia are aggregations of cell bodies outside the CNS.

book_ref.quote: Ganglia are aggregations of cell bodies located outside CNS

blocks.prompt: 85 Which cranial nerves arise from the cerebrum?
blocks.explanation: The first two pairs (olfactory and optic) arise from the cerebrum; the other 10 pairs arise from the brainstem.

book_ref.quote: The first two pairs of cranial nerves (olfactory nerve and optic nerve) arise from cerebrum

blocks.prompt: 86 Cranial nerve VIII is a sensory nerve concerned with:
blocks.explanation: Cranial nerve VIII (sensory) serves hearing and balance.

book_ref.quote: Table: Twelve Pairs of Cranial Nerves & their Functions

blocks.prompt: 87 The cranial nerve that controls the muscles of the tongue is:
blocks.explanation: Cranial nerve XII (motor) controls the muscles of the tongue.

book_ref.quote: Controls the muscles of the tongue

blocks.prompt: 88 Cranial nerve V is a mixed nerve responsible for:

options.text: sensation in the face and control of chewing muscles
movement of the lateral eye muscles

blocks.explanation: Cranial nerve V (mixed) gives sensation in the face and controls the muscles involved in chewing.

book_ref.quote: Sensation in the face; control of the muscles involved in chewing

blocks.prompt: 89 How many pairs of spinal nerves are there, and what is their nature?
blocks.explanation: There are thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves and all are mixed.

book_ref.quote: There are thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves. All spinal nerves are mixed.

blocks.prompt: 90 The ventral root of a spinal nerve contains:
blocks.explanation: The ventral root contains the axons of motor neurons.

book_ref.quote: The ventral root contains the axons of motor neurons

blocks.prompt: 91 The number of pairs of thoracic spinal nerves is:
blocks.explanation: Spinal nerves: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal pair.

book_ref.quote: 12 pairs of thoracic nerves

blocks.prompt: 92 The number of pairs of cervical spinal nerves is:
blocks.explanation: There are 8 pairs of cervical nerves.

book_ref.quote: 8 pairs of cervical nerves

blocks.prompt: 93 The motor pathways of the PNS are made of:
blocks.explanation: The motor pathways make two systems: the somatic nervous system and the autonomic nervous system.

book_ref.quote: The motor pathways make of two systems

blocks.prompt: 94 During a reflex action, the somatic nervous system:

options.text: acts only through the vagus nerve

blocks.explanation: The somatic system is voluntary, but for reflex action it operates without conscious control.

book_ref.quote: For reflex action, the somatic system operates without conscious control

blocks.prompt: 95 The motor neurons of the sympathetic nervous system originate from the:

options.text: thoracic and lumbar regions of spinal cord

blocks.explanation: Sympathetic motor neurons originate from the thoracic and lumbar regions; parasympathetic ones from the brain and sacral region.

book_ref.quote: originate from the thoracic and lumbar regions of spinal cord

blocks.prompt: 96 Many motor neurons of the parasympathetic system are carried in the:
blocks.explanation: Many parasympathetic motor neurons are in the vagus, the tenth cranial nerve.

book_ref.quote: Many of these motor neurons are in vagus (the tenth cranial) nerve

blocks.prompt: 97 The effect of the sympathetic nervous system on the pupil of the eye is:
blocks.explanation: Sympathetic: pupil dilation; parasympathetic: pupil constriction.

book_ref.quote: Table: Effects of Autonomic Nervous System on Body Parts

blocks.prompt: 98 The parasympathetic nervous system causes the urinary bladder to:
blocks.explanation: Sympathetic relaxes the urinary bladder; parasympathetic contracts it.

book_ref.quote: Table: Effects of Autonomic Nervous System on Body Parts

blocks.prompt: 99 The sympathetic nervous system's effect on the blood vessels in skin is:
blocks.explanation: Sympathetic constricts blood vessels in skin (and dilates those in muscles); parasympathetic has no effect on either.

book_ref.quote: Table: Effects of Autonomic Nervous System on Body Parts

blocks.prompt: 100 The simplest receptors, responding to changes in temperature and chemicals in extracellular fluid, are:
blocks.explanation: The simplest receptors are free nerve endings that respond to various stimuli.

book_ref.quote: The simplest receptors are free nerve endings

blocks.prompt: 101 The approximate number of taste buds in humans is:
blocks.explanation: There are about 10,000 taste buds, most between papillae on the tongue.

book_ref.quote: There are about 10,000 taste buds

blocks.prompt: 102 In a taste bud, basal cells function in:
blocks.explanation: A taste bud has receptor cells with hair-like structures and basal cells that make new receptor cells.

book_ref.quote: basal cells (for making new receptor cells)

blocks.prompt: 103 Taste impulses reach the brainstem along cranial nerves:
blocks.explanation: Taste impulses travel along cranial nerves VII, IX and X to the brainstem and then to the taste areas of the cortex.

book_ref.quote: The nerve impulses travel along nerves (cranial nerve VII, IX, and X) and reach brainstem

blocks.prompt: 104 In the nasal epithelium, the cells that act as stem cells to replace old olfactory neurons are:
blocks.explanation: Olfactory neurons lie between supporting cells (protection) and basal cells (stem cells that replace old neurons).

book_ref.quote: basal cells, which act as stem cells to replace old neurons

blocks.prompt: 105 Air-borne chemicals bind to receptor sites on the cilia of olfactory neurons after they:

options.text: dissolve in the mucus of the nasal cavity

blocks.explanation: The cilia project into the moist mucus; air-borne chemicals dissolve in the mucus and bind to receptor sites on the cilia.

book_ref.quote: These cilia project outward into the moist mucus that lines the nasal cavity

blocks.prompt: 106 Receptors of the skin are called:
blocks.explanation: Cutaneous receptors (receptors of the skin) respond to touch, pressure, heat, cold and pain.

book_ref.quote: Different cutaneous receptors (receptors of the skin) respond to touch

blocks.prompt: 107 Pain is defined as a stimulus that:

options.text: causes or is about to cause tissue damage

blocks.explanation: Pain is a stimulus that causes or is about to cause tissue damage.

book_ref.quote: Pain is defined as a stimulus that causes or is about to cause tissue damage

blocks.prompt: 108 Cold receptors in the skin are located:
blocks.explanation: Cold receptors lie immediately below the epidermis; warm receptors lie slightly deeper, in the dermis.

book_ref.quote: Cold receptors are located immediately below the epidermis

blocks.prompt: 109 Thermoreceptors in the hypothalamus monitor the body's core temperature by detecting the temperature of:

options.text: the cerebrospinal fluid in the spinal cord

blocks.explanation: Thermoreceptors in the hypothalamus detect blood temperature and so monitor core temperature.

book_ref.quote: where they detect the temperature of the blood

blocks.prompt: 110 Encapsulated receptors in the upper layer of skin of lips, fingertips, palm and soles that detect light touch and vibration are:
blocks.explanation: Meissner's corpuscles lie in the upper layer of skin and detect light touch and vibration.

book_ref.quote: They detect light touch and vibration.

blocks.prompt: 111 Oval-shaped receptors in the deepest layer of the epidermis that detect light touch are:
blocks.explanation: Merkel cells are oval receptors in the deepest layer of the epidermis, present in touch-sensitive areas like fingertips.

book_ref.quote: Merkel cells are oval-shaped receptors in the deepest layer of epidermis

blocks.prompt: 112 Ruffini endings located in the dermis detect:
blocks.explanation: Ruffini endings are encapsulated endings in the dermis that detect sustained pressure and stretching.

book_ref.quote: They detect sustained pressure and stretching.

blocks.prompt: 113 Hair follicle receptors detect:
blocks.explanation: Hair follicle receptors around the base of hair follicles detect movement of hairs caused by mechanical or thermal stimuli.

book_ref.quote: They detect the movement of hairs

blocks.text: 15.7 Effects of drugs on nervous coordination

blocks.prompt: 114 A drug that alters brain functions, causing changes in mood, perception, consciousness and behaviour, is a:
blocks.explanation: A psychoactive drug alters brain functions, changing mood, perception, consciousness and behaviour.

book_ref.quote: A psychoactive drug is a type of drug that alters brain functions

blocks.prompt: 115 Which statement is correct?

options.text: All narcotics are psychoactive, but not all psychoactive drugs are narcotics

blocks.explanation: All narcotics are psychoactive drugs, but all psychoactive drugs are not narcotics.

book_ref.quote: All narcotics are psychoactive drugs, but all psychoactive drugs are not narcotics

blocks.prompt: 116 A state in which a person relies on a drug physically or emotionally in order to function is called:
blocks.explanation: Dependence is relying on a drug physically or emotionally in order to function; it often results in addiction.

book_ref.quote: Dependence is a state in which a person relies on a drug physically or emotionally

blocks.prompt: 117 A regular caffeine user who stops caffeine abruptly may experience:
blocks.explanation: Regular use leads to tolerance; abrupt stopping can cause withdrawal symptoms such as headaches and fatigue.

book_ref.quote: Regular caffeine use can lead to tolerance

blocks.prompt: 118 Nicotine produces pleasurable feelings by causing release of:
blocks.explanation: Nicotine binds to nicotine receptors in the brain, leading to release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters.

book_ref.quote: These receptors release dopamine and other neurotransmitters to produce pleasurable feelings

blocks.prompt: 119 Drug tolerance develops at the neural level because the brain:

options.text: increases the number of dopamine receptors
reduces the number of dopamine receptors on the postsynaptic neuron

blocks.explanation: Drug molecules block dopamine reabsorption, dopamine accumulates, and the brain reduces postsynaptic dopamine receptors: tolerance.

book_ref.quote: Brain adapts and reduces the number of dopamine receptors on postsynaptic neuron

blocks.prompt: 120 Addictive drug molecules cause dopamine to accumulate in the synaptic cleft by:

options.text: blocking the dopamine reabsorption receptors in the presynaptic neuron

blocks.explanation: The drug molecules block the reabsorption receptors in the presynaptic neuron, so large amounts of dopamine accumulate.

book_ref.quote: The drug molecules block the dopamine reabsorption receptors in presynaptic neuron

blocks.prompt: 121 Drug abuse generally refers to:

options.text: prescribed use of drugs for medical purposes

blocks.explanation: 'Use' is appropriate or prescribed medical use; 'abuse' is inappropriate use of psychoactive drugs.

book_ref.quote: The term "abuse" generally refers to the inappropriate use of psychoactive drugs

blocks.prompt: 122 Heroin is an opioid drug derived from the:
blocks.explanation: Heroin is a highly addictive opioid derived from the opium poppy plant.

book_ref.quote: It is a highly addictive opioid drug that is derived from the opium poppy plant

blocks.prompt: 123 Marijuana and hashish are made from:
blocks.explanation: Cannabis is made from dried flowering tops, leaves and stem of the Indian hemp plant Cannabis sativa; it includes marijuana and hashish.

book_ref.quote: Indian hemp plant Cannabis sativa

blocks.prompt: 124 Among the drugs described, liver diseases are listed as a negative effect of:
blocks.explanation: Alcohol's negative effects include impaired cognitive and motor functions, liver diseases, cardiovascular diseases and mental health disorders.

book_ref.quote: Its negative effects include impaired cognitive and motor functions, liver diseases

blocks.prompt: 125 Nail polish remover and glue are examples of:
blocks.explanation: Inhalants such as nail polish remover and glue are inhaled to produce euphoria, relaxation and altered perception.

book_ref.quote: Inhalants, such as nail polish remover and glue

blocks.prompt: 126 Which of the following is a vascular disorder of the nervous system?
blocks.explanation: Vascular disorders affect blood vessels of brain and spinal cord, e.g. stroke and cerebral venous thrombosis.

book_ref.quote: Examples include stroke and cerebral venous thrombosis

blocks.prompt: 127 A stroke caused by leaking or rupture of a blood vessel in the brain is called:
blocks.explanation: Ischemic stroke: vessels narrowed or blocked; haemorrhagic stroke: a vessel leaks or ruptures.

book_ref.quote: Haemorrhagic stroke occurs when a blood vessel in brain leaks or ruptures

blocks.prompt: 128 Aphasia, a common symptom of stroke, means:
blocks.explanation: Aphasia is the inability to express through words.

book_ref.quote: aphasia (inability to express through words)

blocks.prompt: 129 The most severe and life-threatening form of meningitis is:
blocks.explanation: Bacterial meningitis is the most severe; viral is usually less severe; fungal is rare.

book_ref.quote: Bacterial meningitis is the most severe and life-threatening

blocks.prompt: 130 Fungal meningitis usually occurs in people who:
blocks.explanation: Fungal meningitis is rare and usually occurs in people with weak immune systems; it needs long-term antifungal treatment.

book_ref.quote: Fungal meningitis is rare and usually occurs in people with weak immune systems

blocks.prompt: 131 Spinal cord injury is an example of which type of nervous disorder?
blocks.explanation: Structural disorders result from abnormalities or damage to the physical structure; examples are brain tumour and spinal cord injuries.

book_ref.quote: Examples include brain tumour, and spinal cord injuries

blocks.prompt: 132 A brain tumour can arise from:
blocks.explanation: Brain tumours can arise from glial cells or from the neurons themselves; they may be benign or malignant.

book_ref.quote: Brain tumour can arise from glial cells or from the neurons themselves

blocks.prompt: 133 Migraine and tension headache are examples of:
blocks.explanation: Primary headaches are due to the headache itself, not another cause, e.g. migraine and tension headache.

book_ref.quote: Primary headaches are due to headache itself and not due to another cause

blocks.prompt: 134 A headache with intense, throbbing pain on one side or one region of the head is:
blocks.explanation: Migraine is characterized by intense, throbbing pain on one side or in one region of the head.

book_ref.quote: intense, throbbing pain on one side or in one region of head

blocks.prompt: 135 An autoimmune disease of the CNS in which the myelin sheath is damaged is:
blocks.explanation: Multiple sclerosis damages the myelin sheath, leading to vision loss, pain, fatigue and impaired coordination.

book_ref.quote: autoimmune disease of the CNS in which myelin sheath is damaged

blocks.prompt: 136 Alzheimer's disease is a progressive degenerative brain disorder that leads to:
blocks.explanation: Alzheimer's disease affects memory, thinking and behaviour and leads to dementia in older adults.

book_ref.quote: It leads to dementia in older adults

blocks.prompt: 137 In EEG, the device that magnifies the electrical signals detected by the scalp electrodes is the:
blocks.explanation: Metal electrodes on the scalp are connected to an amplifier that magnifies the signals, recorded as waveforms.

book_ref.quote: These electrodes are connected to an amplifier

blocks.prompt: 138 Which statement about EEG is correct?

options.text: It is painless and needs no sedation or anaesthesia
It uses a strong magnetic field

blocks.explanation: EEG is painless and does not require sedation or anaesthesia; it records the brain's electrical activity.

book_ref.quote: It is painless and does not require sedation or anaesthesia

blocks.prompt: 139 The EEG waves associated with the normal alert state and active thinking are:
blocks.explanation: Beta waves: normal alert state and active thinking; alpha waves: physically and mentally relaxed state.

book_ref.quote: Beta waves are associated with normal alert state and active thinking

blocks.prompt: 140 In a CT scan, the doughnut-shaped machine containing a rotating X-ray tube is called the:
blocks.explanation: The patient slides into a doughnut-shaped gantry whose X-ray tube rotates around the patient.

book_ref.quote: slides into a doughnut-shaped machine called a gantry

blocks.prompt: 141 The basic principle of CT scanning is that different tissues:

options.text: contain different amounts of hydrogen atoms

blocks.explanation: CT is based on different tissues having varying degrees of X-ray absorption.

book_ref.quote: different tissues in body have varying degrees of X-ray absorption

blocks.prompt: 142 MRI is based on the fact that different tissues have varying amounts of:
blocks.explanation: MRI uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves; tissues differ in hydrogen atoms, which have magnetic properties.

book_ref.quote: different tissues in the body have varying amounts of hydrogen atoms

blocks.prompt: 143 Compared with CT (cross-sectional images), MRI uses a computer to construct a:
blocks.explanation: In MRI the receiver's signals are used by a computer to construct a detailed, three-dimensional image.

book_ref.quote: construct a detailed, three-dimensional image of the internal structures
